passages.text: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his entire army and laid siege to the city.
passages.sermon:
Zedekiah was king of Judah.
Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylon.
In the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, the tenth month began.
Nebuchadnezzar gathered his entire army.
Nebuchadnezzar marched to Jerusalem.
Nebuchadnezzar and his army surrounded Jerusalem.
They laid siege to the city.
passages.original: בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַ֠תְּשִׁעִית לְצִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ מֶלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֜ה בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂרִ֗י בָּ֠א נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֨ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֤ל וְכָל־ חֵילוֹ֙ אֶל־ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיָּצֻ֖רוּ עָלֶֽיהָ׃ס

passages.text: And on the ninth day of the fourth month of Zedekiah’s eleventh year, the city was breached.
passages.sermon:
Zedekiah was king of Judah.
He ruled for eleven years.
In the eleventh year of Zedekiah’s reign, something happened.
This event took place in the fourth month.
It happened on the ninth day of that month.
On that day, the city was breached.
Enemies broke through the city walls.
passages.original: בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי־ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ לְצִדְקִיָּ֔הוּ בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרְבִיעִ֖י בְּתִשְׁעָ֣ה לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָבְקְעָ֖ה הָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: Then all the officials of the king of Babylon entered and sat in the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer of Samgar, Nebo-sarsekim the Rabsaris, Nergal-sharezer the Rabmag, and all the rest of the officials of the king of Babylon.
passages.sermon:
The king of Babylon was Nebuchadnezzar.
He had many officials.
All the officials of the king of Babylon entered Jerusalem.
They sat in the Middle Gate of the city.
Nergal-sharezer from Samgar was one of these officials.
Nebo-sarsekim was another official.
Nebo-sarsekim held the title Rabsaris.
Nergal-sharezer the Rabmag was also there.
All the other officials of the king of Babylon were present too.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ כֹּ֚ל שָׂרֵ֣י מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֔ל וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ בְּשַׁ֣עַר הַתָּ֑וֶךְ נֵרְגַ֣ל שַׂר־ אֶ֠צֶר סַֽמְגַּר־ נְב֞וּ שַׂר־ סְכִ֣ים רַב־ סָרִ֗יס נֵרְגַ֤ל שַׂר־ אֶ֙צֶר֙ רַב־ מָ֔ג וְכָל־ שְׁאֵרִ֔ית שָׂרֵ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the soldiers saw them, they fled. They left the city at night by way of the king’s garden, through the gate between the two walls, and they went out along the route to the Arabah.
passages.sermon:
Zedekiah was the king of Judah.
He saw the Babylonian officials enter the city.
All the soldiers with him also saw this.
Zedekiah and all the soldiers decided to flee.
They left the city at night.
They went out by way of the king’s garden.
They passed through the gate between the two walls.
They went out along the road to the Arabah.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר רָ֠אָם צִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֜ה וְכֹ֣ל׀ אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וַֽ֠יִּבְרְחוּ וַיֵּצְא֨וּ לַ֤יְלָה מִן־ הָעִיר֙ דֶּ֚רֶךְ גַּ֣ן הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בְּשַׁ֖עַר בֵּ֣ין הַחֹמֹתָ֑יִם וַיֵּצֵ֖א דֶּ֥רֶךְ הָעֲרָבָֽה׃

passages.text: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They seized him and brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment on him.
passages.sermon:
The army of the Chaldeans chased Zedekiah and his men.
They caught Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho.
They seized Zedekiah.
They brought Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar.
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
They brought Zedekiah to Riblah.
Riblah was in the land of Hamath.
Nebuchadnezzar spoke judgment to Zedekiah.
passages.original: וַיִּרְדְּפ֨וּ חֵיל־ כַּשְׂדִּ֜ים אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם וַיַּשִּׂ֣גוּ אֶת־ צִדְקִיָּהוּ֮ בְּעַֽרְב֣וֹת יְרֵחוֹ֒ וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ וַֽ֠יַּעֲלֻהוּ אֶל־ נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֧ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֛ל רִבְלָ֖תָה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֲמָ֑ת וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ מִשְׁפָּטִֽים׃

passages.text: There at Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and he also killed all the nobles of Judah.
passages.sermon:
The king of Babylon was at Riblah.
He killed the sons of Zedekiah.
Zedekiah saw this happen.
The king of Babylon also killed all the nobles of Judah.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁחַט֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֜ל אֶת־ בְּנֵ֧י צִדְקִיָּ֛הוּ בְּרִבְלָ֖ה לְעֵינָ֑יו וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ חֹרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה שָׁחַ֖ט מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: Then he put out Zedekiah’s eyes and bound him with bronze chains to take him to Babylon.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
He blinded Zedekiah.
He put bronze chains on Zedekiah.
He took Zedekiah to Babylon.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ עֵינֵ֥י צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ עִוֵּ֑ר וַיַּאַסְרֵ֙הוּ֙ בַּֽנְחֻשְׁתַּ֔יִם לָבִ֥יא אֹת֖וֹ בָּבֶֽלָה׃

passages.text: The Chaldeans set fire to the palace of the king and to the houses of the people, and they broke down the walls of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The Chaldeans were a people from Babylon.
The Chaldeans set fire to the king’s palace.
The Chaldeans set fire to the houses of the people.
The Chaldeans broke down the walls of Jerusalem.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ בֵּ֤ית הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וְאֶת־ בֵּ֣ית הָעָ֔ם שָׂרְפ֥וּ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֖ים בָּאֵ֑שׁ וְאֶת־ חֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם נָתָֽצוּ׃

passages.text: Then Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried away to Babylon the remnant of the people who had remained in the city, along with the deserters who had defected to him.
passages.sermon:
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard for the king of Babylon.
He took the people who remained in the city of Jerusalem.
He also took those who had deserted and joined him.
He carried all these people away to Babylon.
passages.original: וְאֵת֩ יֶ֨תֶר הָעָ֜ם הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֣ים בָּעִ֗יר וְאֶת־ הַנֹּֽפְלִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָפְל֣וּ עָלָ֔יו וְאֵ֛ת יֶ֥תֶר הָעָ֖ם הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֑ים הֶגְלָ֛ה נְבֽוּזַר־ אֲדָ֥ן רַב־ טַבָּחִ֖ים בָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: But Nebuzaradan left behind in the land of Judah some of the poor people who had no property, and at that time he gave them vineyards and fields.
passages.sermon:
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard for the king of Babylon.
He left some people in the land of Judah.
These people were poor.
They had no property.
Nebuzaradan gave these poor people vineyards.
He also gave them fields.
He did this on that day.
passages.original: וּמִן־ הָעָ֣ם הַדַּלִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵין־ לָהֶם֙ מְא֔וּמָה הִשְׁאִ֛יר נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֥ן רַב־ טַבָּחִ֖ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּתֵּ֥ן לָהֶ֛ם כְּרָמִ֥ים וִֽיגֵבִ֖ים בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃

passages.text: Now Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had given orders about Jeremiah through Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, saying, “Take him, look after him, and do not let any harm come to him; do for him whatever he says.”
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
Jeremiah was a prophet.
Nebuchadnezzar gave orders about Jeremiah.
He spoke to Nebuzaradan.
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard.
Nebuchadnezzar said, “Take Jeremiah.”
He said, “Watch over him.”
He said, “Do not harm him.”
He said, “Do whatever Jeremiah asks you to do.”
passages.original: וַיְצַ֛ו נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֖ל עַֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ בְּיַ֛ד נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֥ן רַב־ טַבָּחִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר׃ קָחֶ֗נּוּ וְעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ שִׂ֣ים עָלָ֔יו וְאַל־ תַּ֥עַשׂ ל֖וֹ מְא֣וּמָה רָּ֑ע כִּ֗י אם כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ יְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ כֵּ֖ן עֲשֵׂ֥ה עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, Nebushazban the Rabsaris, Nergal-sharezer the Rabmag, and all the captains of the king of Babylon had Jeremiah brought from the courtyard of the guard, and they turned him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, to take him home. So Jeremiah remained among his own people.
passages.sermon:
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard for the king of Babylon.
Nebushazban was the chief officer.
Nergal-sharezer was the chief magician.
All the captains of the king of Babylon acted together.
They sent men to bring Jeremiah out of the courtyard of the guard.
They took Jeremiah from his place of confinement.
They gave Jeremiah to Gedaliah.
Gedaliah was the son of Ahikam.
Ahikam was the son of Shaphan.
Gedaliah was to take Jeremiah to his house.
Jeremiah lived among his own people.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח נְבֽוּזַרְאֲדָ֣ן רַב־ טַבָּחִ֗ים וּנְבֽוּשַׁזְבָּן֙ רַב־ סָרִ֔יס וְנֵרְגַ֥ל שַׂר־ אֶ֖צֶר רַב־ מָ֑ג וְכֹ֖ל רַבֵּ֥י מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶֽל׃ וַיִּשְׁלְחוּ֩ וַיִּקְח֨וּ אֶֽת־ יִרְמְיָ֜הוּ מֵחֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָ֗ה וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ אֶל־ גְּדַלְיָ֙הוּ֙ בֶּן־ אֲחִיקָ֣ם בֶּן־ שָׁפָ֔ן לְהוֹצִאֵ֖הוּ אֶל־ הַבָּ֑יִת וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּת֥וֹךְ הָעָֽם׃ס

passages.text: And while Jeremiah had been confined in the courtyard of the guard, the word of the LORD had come to him: “Go and tell Ebed-melech the Cushite that this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: ‘I am about to fulfill My words against this city for harm and not for good, and on that day they will be fulfilled before your eyes.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet.
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
Jeremiah was confined in the courtyard of the guard.
The LORD gave Jeremiah a message.
The LORD told Jeremiah to go to Ebed-melech.
Ebed-melech was a Cushite.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD is the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD said, “I am bringing my words against this city.
I will bring harm to this city, not good.
You, Ebed-melech, will see these things happen on that day.”
passages.original: וְאֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הָיָ֣ה דְבַר־ יְהוָ֑ה בִּֽהְיֹת֣וֹ עָצ֔וּר בַּחֲצַ֥ר הַמַּטָּרָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃ הָל֣וֹךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ֡ לְעֶבֶד־ מֶ֨לֶךְ הַכּוּשִׁ֜י לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִי אֶת־ דְּבָרַ֜י אֶל־ הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את לְרָעָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א לְטוֹבָ֑ה וְהָי֥וּ לְפָנֶ֖יךָ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃

passages.text: But I will deliver you on that day, declares the LORD, and you will not be delivered into the hands of the men whom you fear.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Ebed-melech the Cushite.
The LORD promised to save Ebed-melech.
The LORD said, “I will deliver you on that day.”
The LORD declared this promise.
You will not be handed over to the men you fear.
You will not fall into their hands.
passages.original: וְהִצַּלְתִּ֥יךָ בַיּוֹם־ הַה֖וּא נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א תִנָּתֵן֙ בְּיַ֣ד הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ אַתָּ֥ה יָג֖וֹר מִפְּנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: For I will surely rescue you so that you do not fall by the sword. Because you have trusted in Me, you will escape with your life like a spoil of war, declares the LORD.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Ebed-melech the Cushite.
The LORD promised to rescue Ebed-melech.
The LORD said, “I will save you.”
“You will not die by the sword.”
“You will escape with your life.”
“Your life will be like a prize taken in war.”
“You have trusted in Me,” says the LORD.
passages.original: כִּ֤י מַלֵּט֙ אֲמַלֶּטְךָ֔ וּבַחֶ֖רֶב לֹ֣א תִפֹּ֑ל וְהָיְתָ֨ה לְךָ֤ נַפְשְׁךָ֙ לְשָׁלָ֔ל כִּֽי־ בָטַ֥חְתָּ בִּ֖י נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס
